answer.evidence: Most first-layer units (0, 3-7, 9-16, 19, 21, 22, 24-26, 28, 30, 31) have weights that look like unstructured initialization noise, all within about ±70, with no coherent patch. A few (0, 10, 16) drift negative and have negative biases, so they are likely dead. The units with clearly learned weights (magnitudes 75-99) fall into two groups. (1) Centred blob detectors: unit 1 (rows ~5-17), unit 8 (rows 5-21), unit 18 (rows 7-17, cols 8-22), unit 20 (rows 6-17, cols 6-16), unit 29 (rows 6-18, cols 5-17) and the broad unit 2. Traced to the output, these are net positive: roughly unit 18 +32k, unit 1 +17.6k, unit 20 +10.9k and unit 8 +9.6k in summed W2·W3 integer products. (2) Surround/ring detectors with negative centres: unit 17 has a centre around -90 at rows 8-17, cols 8-16, and is positive on the top rows 0-6, the bottom rows 22-23 and the right edge. Unit 23 is positive on the top rows 0-3 (mean ~+27), the bottom rows and the left edge, negative in the centre, and is net benign. Unit 27 is a broad positive surround and is net malignant. No unit has a compact, off-centre, high-magnitude patch, edge line or corner marker of the kind that would indicate an artifact. Unit 23's top band is part of a ring-shaped surround pattern (left and bottom edges also positive). Its estimated contribution is small (roughly a quarter or less of the central-nodule pathway), and it points toward benign rather than acting as a dominant switch. The structure is consistent with nodule-versus-surround features rather than a spurious marker.
answer.main_feature: The model mainly responds to bright, dense tissue filling the centre of the crop (a larger, solid nodule), which pushes toward malignant via units 1, 8, 18 and 20. Ring-shaped units (17, 23) that respond to bright surroundings around a dark centre (small or faint nodule) push toward benign.
